title: Governor Braun recognizes 34 Indiana businesses with Century and Half Century awards
text:
Governor Braun recognizes 34 Indiana businesses with Century and Half Century awards
Indiana Governor Mike Braun recognized 34 legacy businesses for their longstanding contributions to the state's economy and communities at a ceremony at the Indiana Statehouse, according to an Aug. 19 announcement. The Governor’s Century and Half Century Business Awards honor Hoosier businesses that have operated for at least 100 or 50 consecutive years, respectively, demonstrating commitment to community service.
“Today is a celebration of these Indiana businesses and a recognition of the dedication and resilience they have shown over the past 50 or 100 years,” said Governor Braun. “These 34 businesses have been powering Indiana's economy for decades and are true examples of the Hoosier spirit and work ethic, demonstrating a remarkable commitment to their crafts, their customers and their communities.”
The awards program has recognized more than 1,300 companies in its 34-year history. This year’s honorees include Charles C. Brandt Construction Co., El Popular, Glovers Ice Cream, LigTel Communications, Lutheran Child and Family Services of Indiana/Kentucky Inc., Smith & Butterfield, The Smith Sawyer Smith Agency, Thiele Heating and Air Conditioning among others in the Century Award category. Businesses honored with the Half Century Award include organizations such as 4C Health, A-1 Realty, American Structurepoint, Ancon Construction, Aurora Emergency Rescue, Back Door Quilts and several others from across various counties in Indiana.
Indiana Secretary of Commerce Chuck Goodrich said, “Thanks to the Governor’s leadership, Indiana is a place where all founders and businesses can grow and thrive. This year’s Century and Half Century Award winners include anchors of Indiana Main Streets, growing innovators and nationally recognized corporations, demonstrating the success and longevity of Hoosier businesses and their impact on the state.”
Braun has contributed to public service through roles on school boards as well as state representation; he also achieved growth of his company into a national entity employing thousands; championed over forty bills that became law during his Senate term; graduated summa cum laude with a degree in economics from Wabash College before earning an MBA from Harvard Business School; won election to the U.S. Senate in 2018 before becoming governor; has been married for forty-nine years raising four children—all according to the official website.
More information about resources available for entrepreneurs can be found at iedc.in.gov/entrepreneurship.
